meta.subtitle: Antimicrobial ICU Reference
meta.disclaimer: Clinical reference only. Verify the current local guideline, microbiology/susceptibility, patient factors and source control. Dose calculators do not replace pharmacist/ID review or TDM.
meta.scope: GitHub-ready core build with Layer 1 reference, Layer 2 ICU dose/renal tools, and initial Layer 3 stewardship/teaching workflows; expand and clinically review before institutional publication.

hpusm.name: HPUSM ASP 2025
hpusm.full: Guide to Antimicrobial Therapy — Antimicrobial Stewardship Programme, HPUSM
hpusm.note: Local HPUSM antimicrobial guidance. Displayed first for local empirical recommendations when applicable.

nag.name: Malaysia NAG — current online
nag.full: National Antimicrobial Guideline, Ministry of Health Malaysia, 4th Edition
nag.note: MOH states NAG is online-only so users receive periodic updates. Official site showed Latest Updates: January 2026 when this build was checked on 2026-09-09.

msic.name: MSIC Adult ICU 2023
msic.full: Guide to Antimicrobial Therapy in the Adult ICU, 4th Edition
msic.note: Adult ICU-focused national reference with PK/PD, RRT, TDM, obesity and special-population appendices.

msidc.name: MSIDC MDR Gram-Negative 2024
msidc.full: Consensus Guidelines on Treatment of Multidrug Resistant Gram Negatives, First Edition
msidc.note: Dedicated Malaysian consensus guidance for AmpC, ESBL, CRE, CRAB, resistant Pseudomonas and Stenotrophomonas.

preg.name: NAG Pregnancy & Lactation 2024
preg.full: Antibiotic in Pregnancy and Lactation, Version 2 July 2024
preg.note: Pregnancy/lactation appendix uses legacy FDA pregnancy categories. Clinical context and current product information still require review.

wellington.name: Wellington ICU Spectrum 2022
wellington.full: Wellington ICU Antibiotic Susceptibilities in Intensive Care
wellington.note: Rapid spectrum guide only; local susceptibility and isolate-specific results supersede expected-spectrum displays.

drugs.name: Meropenem
drugs.quickDose: LD 1 g IV, then 1 g IV q8h by prolonged infusion; CNS/MDR regimen uses 2 g dosing where indicated.
doseNotes: MSIC ICU: standard LD 1 g over 30 min, then 1 g q8h over 4 h.
MSIC ICU: CNS infection/MDR organisms: LD 2 g, then 2 g q8h over 4 h.
Dose-adjust maintenance in renal impairment; loading dose is generally preserved unless source states otherwise.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam exposure; prolonged infusion can improve fT>MIC target attainment in critical illness.
warnings: Broad-spectrum carbapenem: de-escalate when microbiology permits.
Review seizure/neurotoxicity risk in severe renal dysfunction and ensure dose adjustment.

drugs.name: Piperacillin–Tazobactam
drugs.quickDose: MSIC ICU: LD 4.5 g IV, then 4.5 g q6h over 4 h; local disease-specific regimens may use q6–8h.
doseNotes: For q8h administration in the current NAG severe CAP/lung abscess guidance, extended infusion over 3–4 h is specified.
Adjust maintenance dose for renal impairment/RRT.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam exposure; prolonged infusion is useful when higher target attainment is required.
warnings: Does not provide MRSA coverage.
Use local antibiogram and isolate susceptibility; expected spectrum is not a susceptibility result.

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.quickDose: MSIC ICU: LD 2 g IV, then 1–2 g q8–12h over 4 h; severe pneumonia commonly uses 2 g q8h.
doseNotes: Higher dose is used in bacteraemia, endocarditis, meningitis and severe pneumonia in the MSIC renal appendix.
Renal adjustment is important because accumulation increases neurotoxicity risk.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam; extended infusion supports fT>MIC target attainment.
warnings: MSIC notes higher neurotoxicity risk in elderly patients, renal impairment and inappropriate dosing.
No reliable anaerobic coverage; add an anaerobic agent when the syndrome requires it.

drugs.name: Ceftazidime
drugs.quickDose: MSIC ICU: LD 2 g IV, then 1–2 g q8h over 4 h; melioidosis/higher MIC regimen uses 2 g q6h over 4 h.
doseNotes: Renal dose adjustment is required.
Current NAG severe CAP page states ceftazidime is not recommended for empirical CAP because of poor pneumococcal activity.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam; prolonged infusion is used in MSIC ICU dosing.
warnings: Do not infer pneumococcal coverage from “third-generation cephalosporin” label; syndrome-specific guidance matters.

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.quickDose: MSIC ICU: LD 20–25 mg/kg actual body weight (max 2 g/dose), then maintenance guided by renal function and TDM.
doseNotes: Normal renal function: 15–20 mg/kg q12h after loading dose in the MSIC TDM appendix.
AUC24/MIC target 400–600 is shown in the MSIC hypoalbuminaemia appendix; trough 15–20 mg/L is an alternate exposure indicator in selected contexts.
Infusion rate should not exceed 10 mg/min.
drugs.pkpd: Exposure-dependent killing; AUC-guided monitoring is preferred where feasible.
warnings: TDM is required for serious infections and changing renal function.
Vancomycin is inferior to antistaphylococcal β-lactams for MSSA when those agents can be used.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin–Clavulanate
drugs.quickDose: Common adult IV regimen in the source set: 1.2 g q8h; some intra-abdominal/abscess indications use q6h.
doseNotes: Use syndrome-specific regimen and renal adjustment.
warnings: No Pseudomonas coverage.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.quickDose: Disease-specific adult regimens in the source set commonly use 1–2 g IV q24h or 1 g q12h; meningitis uses 2 g q12h.
doseNotes: Select dose by indication rather than using a single universal regimen.
warnings: No Pseudomonas coverage.
Avoid treating AmpC-risk organisms solely from a generic susceptible report without considering inducible resistance and syndrome.

drugs.name: Ampicillin–Sulbactam
drugs.quickDose: For susceptible Acinetobacter: 3 g IV q6h; high-dose sulbactam regimens are used for CRAB in local/MDR guidance.
doseNotes: MSIC renal appendix lists 3 g q6h for Acinetobacter and 9 g q8h over 4 h for carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter.
Local HPUSM targeted CRAB guidance includes high-dose extended infusion in moderate–severe infection.
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam; high-dose sulbactam exposure is the key CRAB concept.
warnings: Does not cover Pseudomonas.
CRAB therapy should be checked against dedicated MDR guidance and susceptibility data.

drugs.name: Cloxacillin
drugs.quickDose: Serious MSSA infection regimens in the source set commonly use 2 g IV q4–6h.
doseNotes: HPUSM states vancomycin should not be used for MSSA when an antistaphylococcal penicillin is appropriate.
warnings: Not active against MRSA.

drugs.name: Gentamicin
drugs.quickDose: Dose is indication- and weight-specific; once-daily regimens are common. Use TDM and renal/RRT guidance.
doseNotes: MSIC TDM guidance uses timed concentrations and more frequent monitoring when renal function changes or nephrotoxic drugs are present.
drugs.pkpd: Concentration-dependent killing; target adequate peak exposure while limiting accumulation.
warnings: Not appropriate monotherapy for Staphylococcus aureus in the Wellington ICU chart.
TDM and renal adjustment are essential.

drugs.name: Amikacin
drugs.quickDose: Weight-based aminoglycoside; dosing interval and redosing require renal/RRT assessment and TDM.
doseNotes: MSIC renal appendix gives RRT-specific regimens; use the TDM workspace for sampling reminders.
warnings: TDM and renal adjustment are essential.

drugs.name: Trimethoprim–Sulfamethoxazole
drugs.quickDose: Dose by TMP component and indication; severe Stenotrophomonas regimens use high-dose TMP-based therapy in the local guidance.
doseNotes: HPUSM targeted Stenotrophomonas: 15 mg/kg/day TMP component in 3–4 divided doses.
MSIC organism-specific ICU table uses 5 mg/kg TMP component q8h for Stenotrophomonas. Keep source-specific regimens separate.
drugs.pkpd: Exposure depends on indication; dose calculations are based on trimethoprim component.

pregnancy.lactation: Present in human milk; not recommended in infants <2 months

warnings: Monitor potassium and renal function in high-dose therapy.
Do not merge differing source doses without considering indication and severity.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.quickDose: Severe CAP regimens in the source set commonly use 500 mg IV/PO q24h as atypical coverage.
doseNotes: Duration varies by syndrome and confirmed pathogen.
drugs.pkpd: Useful for atypical respiratory pathogens; not a broad Gram-negative ICU agent.
warnings: Consider QT interval and interacting QT-prolonging drugs.

drugs.name: Ertapenem
drugs.quickDose: 1 g IV q24h in normal renal function; selected ESBL syndromes use ertapenem when antipseudomonal coverage is unnecessary.
doseNotes: MSIC notes that ertapenem is not recommended in critically ill patients with hypoalbuminaemia.
warnings: No Pseudomonas coverage.
Avoid as default carbapenem in critically ill hypoalbuminaemic patients per MSIC ICU guidance.

drugs.name: Imipenem–Cilastatin
drugs.quickDose: MSIC ICU: LD 1 g IV, then imipenem 500 mg q6h over 4 h; renal adjustment required.
doseNotes: Proteus spp are intrinsically less susceptible/resistant to imipenem in the MSIC organism-specific table.
warnings: Renal dose adjustment is important.

conditions.name: Hospital-/Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia
conditions.summary: Treat as a syndrome with acquisition timing, MDR risk, respiratory sampling and rapid 48–72 h reassessment. Do not interpret a positive respiratory culture without clinical context.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Obtain a good-quality endotracheal aspirate/non-invasive respiratory specimen when possible
Assess need for MRSA and MDR Gram-negative coverage using local epidemiology

recommendations.label: Early onset (2–4 days)
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h

recommendations.label: Late onset (≥5 days)
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h ± vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h
alternative: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h ± vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg q8–12h

recommendations.label: No MDR risk factors
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h OR ceftriaxone 1 g IV q12h
alternative: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h OR piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h

recommendations.label: MDR risk factors — Gram-negative coverage
preferred: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h OR piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h
alternative: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h OR imipenem 500 mg IV q6h when clinically appropriate

recommendations.label: Specific MDR phenotype
preferred: ESBL: meropenem/imipenem; MRSA: vancomycin; CRAB/CRE require phenotype-directed therapy
alternative: Use dedicated MDR guidance and susceptibility results
recommendations.duration: Usually 7 days; longer only for delayed response or specific complications

why: MDR risk factors materially change empirical coverage.
MSIC notes Acinetobacter, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa among common ICU isolates in the cited MRIC report.
Aim for ≤7 days in uncomplicated response and de-escalate with microbiology.

conditions.name: Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia
conditions.summary: Severe CAP requires severity assessment, atypical coverage when appropriate, and escalation to antipseudomonal therapy only when Pseudomonas risk is present.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Assess CAP severity (e.g. CURB-65/SMART-COP) and ICU need
Assess strong Pseudomonas risk and recent healthcare/antibiotic exposure

recommendations.label: Severe pneumonia (CURB65 >3)
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h when Pseudomonas risk + azithromycin 500 mg IV/PO q24h
alternative: Use syndrome-/risk-specific alternative from local guidance

recommendations.label: Severe CAP — usual pathogens
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h + azithromycin 500 mg IV q24h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV q12h OR cefotaxime 2 g IV q8h + levofloxacin/moxifloxacin
recommendations.duration: Usually 5–7 days for β-lactam component; atypical duration varies

recommendations.label: If Pseudomonas risk
preferred: Cefepime 2 g IV q8h
alternative: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h

why: Current NAG also emphasizes local antibiogram and pseudomonal risk before antipseudomonal therapy; open the live NAG page for the latest national wording.

conditions.name: Bacterial Meningitis
conditions.summary: Time-critical syndrome: obtain blood cultures/CSF when safe without delaying treatment. Dose selection must achieve CNS exposure.
before: Obtain blood cultures promptly
Perform lumbar puncture when safe; do not delay time-critical antimicrobials for prolonged investigations
Assess need for imaging before LP based on neurological features
Consider age/immunocompromise and Listeria risk

recommendations.label: Adult empirical local regimen
preferred: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + ampicillin 2 g IV q4h
alternative: Use allergy/pathogen-specific regimen
notes: Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg q6h for 2–4 days is listed in the source.

why: CNS dosing differs from routine dosing because adequate CSF/tissue exposure is required.

conditions.name: Brain Abscess
conditions.summary: Treat with prolonged therapy plus source control/neurosurgical assessment when indicated.
before: Obtain blood cultures and neurosurgical/microbiology specimens when feasible
Assess contiguous ENT/dental source, haematogenous source and prior neurosurgery
Plan source control/drainage where appropriate

recommendations.label: Local empirical regimen
preferred: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
alternative: Cefotaxime 2 g IV q4–6h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 4–8 weeks; source lists minimum 2 weeks IV

conditions.name: Aspiration Pneumonia
conditions.summary: Distinguish aspiration pneumonitis from bacterial aspiration infection; syndrome and healthcare exposure determine whether broad Gram-negative/anaerobic coverage is needed.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Assess for abscess/empyema and need for drainage
Clarify community vs healthcare-associated aspiration

recommendations.label: Local aspiration pneumonia
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h ± metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: Use clinical context; distinguish from lung abscess duration

recommendations.label: Healthcare-associated aspiration / lung abscess
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h OR cefepime 2 g IV q8h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
alternative: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h OR imipenem 500 mg IV q6h
recommendations.duration: Aspiration pneumonia 7 days; lung abscess minimum 4 weeks

conditions.name: Lung Abscess / Empyema
conditions.summary: Antibiotics are only one component; drainage/source control is central when a pleural collection is present.
before: Obtain appropriate cultures before antimicrobials when this does not cause harmful delay
Review previous microbiology and recent antimicrobial exposure
Check allergy and previous serious antimicrobial adverse reactions
Check renal function and whether renal replacement therapy is being used
Obtain pleural fluid/pus culture where feasible
Arrange drainage for empyema/complicated collection

recommendations.label: Local lung abscess
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 28–42 days in the source; step down when clinically improved

recommendations.label: Healthcare-associated aspiration/lung abscess
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g q6h OR cefepime 2 g q8h + metronidazole 500 mg q8h
alternative: Meropenem 1 g q8h OR imipenem 500 mg q6h
recommendations.duration: Lung abscess minimum 4 weeks; response/imaging dependent

conditions.name: Acute Pyelonephritis
conditions.summary: Obtain urine culture before treatment where possible and distinguish uncomplicated from complicated UTI/urosepsis.
before: Urinalysis and urine culture
Blood cultures if systemically unwell
Assess obstruction/stone and need for urgent source control
Check renal function and pregnancy status

recommendations.label: Local adult pyelonephritis
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg/24h
alternative: Cefuroxime 750–1500 mg IV q8h

conditions.name: Urosepsis
conditions.summary: Treat sepsis and assess for obstructed infected urinary tract, which requires urgent source control.
before: Blood cultures and urine culture
Assess urinary obstruction/stone and need for urgent drainage
Review previous urinary isolates and ESBL/CRE risk
Check renal function

recommendations.label: Local empirical regimen
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h
alternative: Cefepime 1 g IV q8h

conditions.name: Septic Shock — Undifferentiated Empirical Antibiotic
conditions.summary: Use this only as an undifferentiated local starting reference. The final empirical regimen should be driven by suspected source, previous cultures, recent antibiotics and local resistance patterns.
before: Obtain blood cultures before antimicrobials if this does not delay treatment
Identify likely source and source control requirement
Review prior cultures/colonisation and recent antibiotics
Assess allergy, renal function and local resistance patterns

recommendations.label: Non-diabetic — undifferentiated local guide
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h
alternative: Source-directed therapy may supersede this
recommendations.duration: Revise/de-escalate at 48–72 h based on cultures and clinical source

recommendations.label: Diabetic — undifferentiated local guide
preferred: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Source-directed therapy may supersede this

why: The MSIC ICU guide stresses rapid microbiological sampling, appropriate empirical coverage, PK/PD optimisation, source control and de-escalation.

conditions.name: Necrotising Fasciitis
conditions.summary: Surgical source control is time-critical. Antimicrobials should not delay debridement.
before: Urgent surgical review and debridement/source control
Blood cultures and deep operative tissue cultures
Assess shock and organ support requirements

recommendations.label: Local empirical regimen
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h ± clindamycin 600–900 mg IV q8h
alternative: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6h
recommendations.duration: 7–14 days in the source; tailor to source control and clinical response

conditions.name: Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infection
conditions.summary: Early source control plus appropriate antimicrobial therapy are the core management principles.
before: Obtain blood cultures in septic patients
Obtain operative/peritoneal specimens when source control is performed
Assess whether infection is community- or hospital-acquired
Prioritise source control

recommendations.label: Principle
preferred: Use narrower therapy for community-acquired IAI when appropriate; hospital-acquired IAI more often requires MDR-aware coverage
alternative: Tailor to local epidemiology and culture
recommendations.duration: After adequate source control, duration should be limited and response-driven

conditions.name: Infective Endocarditis
conditions.summary: Empirical therapy depends on native vs prosthetic valve and must be narrowed to organism-specific treatment when cultures are available.
before: Obtain at least 2 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics when feasible
Clarify native vs prosthetic valve and timing of valve surgery
Assess for heart failure, embolic/metastatic infection and need for echocardiography
Check renal function before aminoglycoside/vancomycin-containing regimens

recommendations.label: Native valve — empirical, culture pending
preferred: Ampicillin 2 g IV q4h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h PLUS/MINUS cloxacillin 2 g IV q4h
alternative: Penicillin allergy: vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q8–12h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h
recommendations.duration: Source table lists 28–42 days depending on organism; definitive duration must follow organism/valve-specific guidance.

recommendations.label: Prosthetic valve — empirical, culture pending
preferred: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q8–12h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h PLUS rifampicin 300–450 mg PO q12h
recommendations.duration: Definitive duration depends on organism and prosthetic-valve context.

recommendations.label: Prosthetic valve <12 months — empirical
preferred: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV q12h PLUS gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h PLUS rifampicin 300–450 mg PO q12h
alternative: Optional cefepime 2 g IV q8h OR piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h when non-HACEK Gram-negative coverage is indicated by local epidemiology

why: Blood cultures before treatment are central to pathogen-directed therapy.
Aminoglycoside/vancomycin regimens require toxicity monitoring and should be narrowed when cultures permit.

conditions.name: Cellulitis
conditions.summary: HPUSM ASP 2025 stratifies cellulitis by severity and primarily targets staphylococci and streptococci.
before: Assess severity and systemic toxicity
Look for abscess/necrotising infection or another source requiring drainage/source control
Review allergy history and renal function if IV broad-spectrum therapy is being considered

recommendations.label: Mild
preferred: Cloxacillin 500 mg PO q6h
alternative: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 625 mg PO q8h

recommendations.label: Moderate
preferred: Cloxacillin 500 mg PO q6h
alternative: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6–8h

recommendations.label: Severe
preferred: Piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6–8h
alternative: Ampicillin–sulbactam 3 g IV q6–8h

why: Severe disease broadens empirical coverage; abscess or necrotising infection requires a different pathway.

conditions.name: Osteomyelitis
conditions.summary: HPUSM separates acute empirical treatment from chronic disease, where surgical debridement and tissue culture guide therapy.
before: Obtain appropriate deep/tissue cultures where feasible
Assess for surgical debridement/source control
Review prior microbiology, implants and chronicity

recommendations.label: Acute osteomyelitis
preferred: Cloxacillin 2 g IV q6h
alternative: Clindamycin 600 mg IV q8h
recommendations.duration: 2–4 weeks IV followed by oral therapy; total 6 weeks in the source table.

recommendations.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
preferred: Empirical treatment is not indicated; surgical debridement and tissue culture/susceptibility guide treatment.
recommendations.duration: Source table lists 6 weeks to 3 months depending on context.

why: Chronic osteomyelitis is a source-control and culture-directed problem rather than an empirical-antibiotic-only problem.

conditions.name: Complicated Urinary Tract Infection
conditions.summary: HPUSM ASP 2025 gives a simple local empirical regimen for complicated UTI; resistance phenotype should redirect to the dedicated ESBL/AmpC/CRE pathway when present.
before: Obtain urine culture before antibiotics when feasible
Assess obstruction/stones and need for source control
Review previous urine cultures and recent antimicrobials
Check renal function

recommendations.label: Empirical
preferred: Amoxicillin–clavulanate 1.2 g IV q6h
alternative: Cefuroxime 750–1500 mg IV q8h

why: Known ESBL/AmpC/CRE changes the preferred treatment and should not be handled by the uncomplicated empirical card.

conditions.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii Pneumonia
conditions.summary: MSIC ICU provides pathogen-specific therapy for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in severe community-acquired pneumonia pathways.
before: Confirm immunocompromised context and obtain appropriate diagnostic specimens where feasible
Check renal function, potassium and blood counts before high-dose trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole
Assess whether adjunctive corticosteroid criteria are met

recommendations.label: Preferred
preferred: Trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg (TMP component) IV q6–8h
alternative: Pentamidine 4 mg/kg IV daily OR primaquine 30 mg PO q24h PLUS clindamycin 600–900 mg IV q8h

why: High-dose TMP-SMX is weight-based on the trimethoprim component and requires toxicity monitoring.

conditions.name: Leptospirosis
conditions.summary: Both HPUSM and MSIC provide Malaysian treatment regimens. Their steroid statements are not identical and are therefore shown separately.
before: Assess organ involvement and severity, including AKI, respiratory failure, hypotension and arrhythmia
Send appropriate diagnostic testing without delaying treatment when clinical suspicion is high
Check renal and hepatic function

recommendations.label: Mild
preferred: Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 5–7 days
alternative: Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days

recommendations.label: Moderate to severe
preferred: Benzylpenicillin 1.5 million units IV q6h
alternative: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
notes: HPUSM source states to add steroid for all severe leptospirosis.

recommendations.label: Severe disease
preferred: Benzylpenicillin 1.5 million units IV q6h OR ceftriaxone 1 g IV q12h
notes: MSIC source states there is insufficient evidence to support routine corticosteroids in pulmonary haemorrhage.

recommendations.label: Mild disease
preferred: Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days OR doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 5–7 days OR amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h for 7 days

why: The source conflict on corticosteroid use is deliberately not reconciled by the app.

conditions.name: Melioidosis
conditions.summary: MSIC describes a prolonged two-phase treatment strategy: an IV intensive phase followed by oral eradication therapy, with duration determined by infection site and severity.
before: Obtain cultures; culture is the diagnostic mainstay
Look for deep-seated abscesses and consider CT/ultrasound abdomen/pelvis in culture-positive disease
Assess need for drainage or surgical intervention
Check renal function and TMP-SMX contraindications/interactions

recommendations.label: Initial intensive phase
preferred: Meropenem 1 g IV q8h (2 g q8h for CNS infection) OR imipenem 500 mg IV q6h
alternative: Ceftazidime 2 g IV q6h
recommendations.duration: At least 2 weeks; longer for pneumonia with ICU admission/bacteraemia, deep collections, osteomyelitis, CNS or arterial infection.
notes: Optional TMP-SMX is added in selected sites such as cutaneous disease, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, CNS infection and deep collections in the cited guide.

recommendations.label: Duration framework
preferred: Intensive-phase duration and eradication-phase duration are site-specific; the cited table ranges from 2 to 8 weeks intensive therapy and 3 to 6 months eradication therapy for many listed foci.
recommendations.duration: Use the site-specific melioidosis duration table.

why: Severe disease, deep infection and CNS/vascular involvement require longer treatment than uncomplicated infection.

conditions.name: Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infection / CRBSI
conditions.summary: HPUSM provides local empirical options for central-catheter and haemodialysis-catheter infection; definitive duration depends on the organism and catheter strategy.
before: Obtain blood cultures before antibiotics when feasible
Identify catheter type and assess whether catheter removal is required
Review prior microbiology and MRSA/MDR risk
Check renal function before vancomycin/ceftazidime dosing

recommendations.label: Central catheter
preferred: Cloxacillin 2 g IV q4–6h
recommendations.duration: 7–10 days in the local table; definitive duration depends on organism and clinical context.

recommendations.label: Haemodialysis catheter / MRSA-risk context
preferred: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV PLUS ceftazidime 2 g IV q24h
recommendations.duration: 10–14 days in the local table; duration depends on organism isolated from blood culture.

why: Device/source control and pathogen-specific therapy are central to management.

organisms.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
notes: Expected-spectrum table includes activity from selected antipseudomonal β-lactams and aminoglycosides; susceptibility testing remains decisive.

organisms.name: Acinetobacter baumannii
notes: Common ICU healthcare-associated pathogen; colonisation is frequent, so infection-vs-colonisation assessment is essential.

resistance.name: ESBL-Producing Enterobacterales
resistance.summary: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase phenotype. Treatment depends on infection site, severity and susceptibility; avoid treating the resistance label without the clinical syndrome.

sourceCards.title: Local severe/critical illness signal
sourceCards.text: HPUSM targeted guidance uses ertapenem for selected severe infection and meropenem/imipenem for critically ill/intubated ICU patients; hypoalbuminaemia and site matter.

sourceCards.title: Dedicated MDR guidance
sourceCards.text: MSIDC separates uncomplicated cystitis, pyelonephritis/cUTI and infection outside the urinary tract, with susceptibility confirmation and carbapenem-sparing options where appropriate.

resistance.name: AmpC β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacterales
resistance.summary: AmpC risk changes interpretation of β-lactam susceptibility. Site and susceptibility determine whether cefepime or a carbapenem is preferred.

sourceCards.title: Dedicated AmpC section
sourceCards.text: The MSIDC guideline provides site-specific treatment and emphasises susceptibility confirmation; cefepime is a key option in appropriate susceptible infections.

resistance.name: Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales
resistance.summary: CRE is heterogeneous. Determine whether carbapenemase is present and identify the enzyme (e.g. NDM/MBL, KPC, OXA-48-like) because this can change active options.

sourceCards.title: Local framework
sourceCards.text: HPUSM describes CRE as carbapenem-resistant and/or carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales and notes NDM as a common Malaysian carbapenemase; first distinguish infection from colonisation/contamination and assess severity.

sourceCards.title: Dedicated CRE section
sourceCards.text: Use the MSIDC CRE treatment section for phenotype-/site-specific definitive therapy and infection-control recommendations.

resistance.name: Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
resistance.summary: CRAB management requires infection-vs-colonisation assessment, high-dose sulbactam-based therapy in many Malaysian regimens, severity stratification and susceptibility review.

sourceCards.title: Local targeted therapy
sourceCards.text: HPUSM lists ampicillin–sulbactam for susceptible/mild CRAB and high-dose 9 g q8h extended infusion for moderate–severe disease, with additional agents considered according to the regimen and approval.

sourceCards.title: Dedicated CRAB guidance
sourceCards.text: Use MSIDC Section 4 for current CRAB treatment and infection-control details.

resistance.name: MDR / DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa
resistance.summary: Use site, severity and in-vitro activity. DTR Pseudomonas should trigger dedicated MDR guidance rather than automatic carbapenem escalation.

sourceCards.title: Local targeted therapy
sourceCards.text: HPUSM lists gentamicin and ceftolozane–tazobactam among options for MDR/XDR/DTR Pseudomonas, with combination/intensity varying by severity and susceptibility.

sourceCards.title: Dedicated Pseudomonas section
sourceCards.text: MSIDC Section 5 provides MDR/DTR Pseudomonas epidemiology, infection prevention and treatment.

resistance.name: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia
resistance.summary: Intrinsically resistant to carbapenems. Distinguish colonisation from infection and use susceptibility/site/severity to select therapy.

sourceCards.title: Local targeted therapy
sourceCards.text: HPUSM first-line targeted therapy is trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole dosed by TMP component; ceftazidime is listed when TMP-SMX is contraindicated.

sourceCards.title: Dedicated Stenotrophomonas section
sourceCards.text: MSIDC Section 6 provides treatment and infection-prevention guidance.

resistance.name: Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus
resistance.summary: MRSA is resistant to usual antistaphylococcal β-lactams because of altered PBP2a. Use local MRSA risk/prevalence and syndrome severity to decide empirical coverage.

sourceCards.title: Local guidance
sourceCards.text: HPUSM recommends vancomycin for empirical therapy when MRSA risk is high/severe and for confirmed MRSA; it states vancomycin is inferior to cloxacillin for MSSA.

resistance.name: Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus
resistance.summary: HPUSM notes MSSA causes community and hospital-acquired bloodstream/invasive infection and that vancomycin is inferior to anti-staphylococcal penicillins such as cloxacillin for MSSA.

sourceCards.title: Local HPUSM principle
sourceCards.text: Use an anti-staphylococcal penicillin such as cloxacillin for susceptible S. aureus rather than continuing vancomycin solely for convenience; complicated MSSA infection warrants ID consultation.

meropenem.normal: LD 1 g IV over 30 min → MD 1 g q8h over 4 h
meropenem.high: CNS/MDR: LD 2 g → MD 2 g q8h over 4 h

rrt.HD: 500 mg q24h + 250 mg after dialysis (CNS/MDR: 1 g q24h + 500 mg after dialysis)

piperacillin-tazobactam.normal: LD 4.5 g IV over 30 min → MD 4.5 g q6h over 4 h

cefepime.normal: LD 2 g IV over 30 min → MD 1–2 g q8–12h over 4 h

ceftazidime.normal: LD 2 g IV over 30 min → MD 1–2 g q8h over 4 h
ceftazidime.high: Melioidosis/higher MIC: MD 2 g q6h over 4 h
ceftazidime.note: High-dose melioidosis/higher-MIC renal schedules differ; open the source before using high-dose regimen in renal failure.

imipenem.normal: LD 1 g IV over 30 min → MD 500 mg q6h over 4 h

ertapenem.note: MSIC advises against ertapenem in critically ill patients with hypoalbuminaemia.

bins.text: Dose requires source review; table extraction is not sufficiently clear for a safe automatic recommendation.

vancomycin.normal: LD 20–25 mg/kg actual body weight (max 2 g) → MD 15–20 mg/kg q12h in normal renal function; TDM required.

bins.text: LD 20–25 mg/kg; MD 15–20 mg/kg q12h; obtain AUC/TDM levels per protocol.
LD 20–25 mg/kg; MD 15–20 mg/kg q24h; TDM.
LD 20–25 mg/kg, then redose based on TDM.

rrt.HD: LD 20–25 mg/kg, then TDM; many patients require 5–10 mg/kg post-HD supplemental dose.
rrt.CVVH: LD 20–25 mg/kg; maintenance depends on MIC/effluent rate and TDM.
rrt.CVVHD: LD 20–25 mg/kg; maintenance depends on MIC/effluent rate and TDM.
rrt.CVVHDF: LD 20–25 mg/kg; maintenance depends on MIC/effluent rate and TDM.

vancomycin.note: Use actual body weight for vancomycin loading. AUC-guided monitoring is preferred where available.

checklist: Functional GI tract and reliable absorption
Oral option with adequate bioavailability and spectrum
No syndrome/source-specific reason to continue IV
Document total duration and follow-up plan
